new_findings.title: The wrong-root guidance is inaccurate for XP-PKG-004, whose absence assertions pass vacuously under any root
criterion_or_requirement: none directly - accuracy of the candidate's own anti-misreading guidance, introduced by the F-005 repair
affected_sections: fixtures README, 'Running the cases against these fixtures', final paragraph

evidence.description: Under the fixtures root: XP-PKG-001 3x MISMATCH, XP-PKG-002 5x MISMATCH, XP-PKG-003 8x MISMATCH, XP-PKG-004 COMPLETED with 2x MATCH, XP-PKG-005 4x INDETERMINATE
The guidance says 'Under this root the XP-PKG-* cases correctly MISMATCH, because the fixtures root has no SKILL.md.' That is accurate for three of five cases and wrong for two.

new_findings.impact: Narrow but real, and the same class of hazard the rest of the file works to close. XP-PKG-004's assertions are path_absent on scripts and agents, which are trivially absent from the fixtures root, so the case reports COMPLETED with 2 MATCH against a tree that is not the package. The file's own advice - check the execution_status of every row - does not catch it, because that status is COMPLETED rather than COULD_NOT_RUN. A reader who ran only the fixtures invocation could count XP-PKG-004 as coverage of the no-scripts policy check. An absence assertion passes vacuously anywhere the thing is absent.
new_findings.uncertainty: none on the observation. Whether it is worth an assertion change or only a wording change is the author's call; the wording change alone closes the demonstrated misreading.
new_findings.recommendation: Amend both notes to distinguish the three behaviours - XP-PKG-001..003 mismatch here because there is no SKILL.md; XP-PKG-004's absence assertions pass vacuously against any tree and prove nothing under this root; XP-PKG-005 is INDETERMINATE on mode - and state that none of the five is coverage under this root. Optionally add a path_present anchor assertion (for example on SKILL.md) to XP-PKG-004 so the case cannot complete against a tree that is not the package.
new_findings.regression_note: This text did not exist before the repair; it arrived with the F-005 fix. It is a new, lower-severity defect in new material, surfaced by rerunning the documented invocation rather than assuming it.

ev_s_007_decision.author_position: Declined to carry the evaluator's EV-S-007 into the package. Argued in XP-PKG-003 notes and derivation.json not_copied that unfilled templates correctly hold placeholders, so authoring that assertion would record a healthy package as defective; XP-PKG-003 asserts template presence instead, and placeholder detection stays on a produced artifact where XP-C-004 covers it.
ev_s_007_decision.evaluator_judgement: AGREE. EV-S-007 was an evaluator-side probe whose expected result I declared in prose and interpreted myself. That is defensible for a one-off probe and poor in a durable case file: the runner emits no expected-versus-observed comparison, so a standing assertion whose healthy-package result is MISMATCH inverts the file's reading convention and would train a later reader to skim past mismatches. Separating 'the template is present' from 'a produced report has no placeholders' is the cleaner split and matches the contract's own package-versus-outputs distinction.
ev_s_007_decision.residual_gap: Nothing now detects an assets/ template accidentally shipped pre-filled - the inverse defect. Narrow: the templates are byte-identical to the governing docs/mvp sources, derivation.json records those digests, and this recheck verified all 11 destination digests, so drift would be caught by the provenance record rather than by a case. If a case is ever wanted, the right shape is digest equality against the recorded derivation digest, not a placeholder assertion.
